sentences.zh: 编程砸谈，第44期。

sentences.en: Logo, scratch Lego.
sentences.zh: Logo，草拟乐高。

sentences.en: Take it away, Patrick.
sentences.zh: 开始吧，帕特里克。

sentences.en: I need to have an answer to how many monitors should I have at work.
sentences.zh: 我需要得出个结论：工作时我到底该用几个显示器。

sentences.en: How many monitors does it take to get to the center of a programming problem?
sentences.zh: 究竟要几个显示器才能直击编程问题的核心？

sentences.en: So I feel like I need more.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我需要更多显示器。

sentences.en: Right now I have, or maybe I need bigger monitors.
sentences.zh: 我现在有，或者说我可能需要更大的显示器。

sentences.en: Oh, maybe that's the difference, the size of the monitor or the number of the monitors.
sentences.zh: 哦，也许这才是区别所在，显示器的大小或显示器的数量。

sentences.en: So what do you have right now?
sentences.zh: 那你现在用的是什么？

sentences.en: So right now I have two 24-inch monitors.
sentences.zh: 我现在用的是两个24英寸的显示器。

sentences.en: Two 24, okay.
sentences.zh: 两个24寸的，好的。

sentences.en: And like side-by-side, and I have them on like adjustable arms, and I have them both in landscape mode.
sentences.zh: 就像并排摆放的那种，我把它们装在可调节支架上，两个都设成了横屏模式。

sentences.en: Okay, right.
sentences.zh: 行，对。

sentences.en: And so that's pretty good because the way I have it set up is like, so I run Ubuntu, so I have like the virtual desktop side-by-side.
sentences.zh: 这感觉挺不错的，因为我的设置方式是这样的，我用的是Ubuntu，所以我有并排的虚拟桌面。

sentences.en: I only use two.
sentences.zh: 我只用两个。

sentences.en: And on the first one I have like email and like docs and stuff, you know, kind of on two windows so I can have my email up all the time when I'm on that window or whatever.
sentences.zh: 第一个屏幕上我放了电子邮件、文档之类的内容，你知道的，分在两个窗口里，这样我用那个窗口或干别的时，邮箱就能一直挂在上面。

sentences.en: And the second one I typically have like a browser in one window,
sentences.zh: 第二个屏幕我通常在一个窗口里放浏览器，

sentences.en: documentation, console, command line, and then the other one my IDE.
sentences.zh: 文档、控制台、命令行，然后在另一个窗口放IDE。

sentences.en: So the second monitor is like a split screen, and the first one is just email or something like that?
sentences.zh: 所以第二个显示器是分屏的，而第一个只是用来放邮箱之类的内容？

sentences.en: Well, so like on my second virtual environment, yeah, the first one, the left side is like Eclipse, and then the second one is like my command line
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，就比如在我的第二个虚拟环境里，左边是Eclipse，然后右边是我的命令行

sentences.en: or like documentation in the browser or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者浏览器里的文档之类的。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So I have two.
sentences.zh: 所以我用的是两个。

sentences.en: But then, yeah, like you pointed out, now I don't have space for my email.
sentences.zh: 但接着，正如你所指出的，现在我的邮箱没地方放了。

sentences.en: And so maybe that's good because I don't look at my email, but I feel like I need four monitors.
sentences.zh: 也许这样挺好，因为我不怎么看邮件，但我感觉我需要四个显示器。

sentences.en: Like I feel like I need two more up above for like, you know, so I can have like my console in one,
sentences.zh: 就像我觉得上方还需要两个，你知道的，这样我就可以在一个上面放控制台，

sentences.en: my web browser that's like doing documentation in the other, and my email in the fourth.
sentences.zh: 另一个放用来查文档的网页浏览器，第四个放邮箱。

sentences.en: So I feel like I – but maybe I could just get a bigger one.
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉我——不过也许我换个大一点的就行了。

sentences.en: Like some people have the 30-inch monitors at work.
sentences.zh: 就像有些人工作时用30英寸的显示器。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: But then I feel like it's too – like the tall is wasted.
sentences.zh: 但那样的话我又觉得太——感觉纵向空间被浪费了。

sentences.en: Like I don't need really that height.
sentences.zh: 就是我其实不需要那么高。

sentences.en: See, I feel like this is one of those like thing that sort of bifurcates people.
sentences.zh: 你看，我觉得这是那种容易把人分成两派的问题。

sentences.en: Like some people are zero-inbox people.
sentences.zh: 就像有些人信奉“收件箱清空”原则。

sentences.en: Some people have like 40,000 unread messages, right?
sentences.zh: 有些人有4万条未读消息，对吧？

sentences.en: That would be me.
sentences.zh: 那肯定就是我了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm actually a zero-inbox person.
sentences.zh: 对，其实我是个信奉收件箱清空的人。

sentences.en: So some people are like – you know, it's like some people like Skittles.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人就——你知道的，就像有人喜欢彩虹糖。

sentences.en: Some people like M&Ms.
sentences.zh: 有人喜欢M&M豆。

sentences.en: I don't know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，随便吧。

sentences.en: But this is one of those things.
sentences.zh: 但这就是这类事情之一。

sentences.en: Like I only have one monitor, and everybody kind of – like that gives me a hard time.
sentences.zh: 我只用一个显示器，每个人都觉得——这让我很难办。

sentences.en: But like every now and then someone says, hey, why don't you get a second monitor?
sentences.zh: 但时不时总会有人说，嘿，你为什么不弄个副屏呢？

sentences.en: Or hey, you know, you have your laptop screen.
sentences.zh: 或者，嘿，你看，你笔记本屏幕上。

sentences.en: You just have a picture of your family on it.
sentences.zh: 只放了一张家人的照片。

sentences.en: And I just – for some reason,
sentences.zh: 而我只是——出于某种原因，

sentences.en: I cannot adopt more than one screen into my workflow.
sentences.zh: 我的工作流里就是没法接受一个以上的屏幕。

sentences.en: Even like those virtual screens.
sentences.zh: 甚至连那些虚拟屏幕也一样。

sentences.en: I've started to get into the virtual screens where like on the MacBook Pro, you can use three fingers and swipe.
sentences.zh: 我最近开始尝试虚拟屏幕了，就像在MacBook Pro上，你可以用三指轻扫。

sentences.en: If you do the three-finger swipe, then you go to other virtual screens.
sentences.zh: 如果你做三指轻扫，就能切换到其他虚拟屏幕。

sentences.en: And I've started doing like my, you know, music.
sentences.zh: 我开始用它来搞，你知道的，音乐。

sentences.en: Like I'll have Twitch streaming music on one virtual screen.
sentences.zh: 比如我会在一个虚拟屏幕上挂着Twitch的音乐直播。

sentences.en: But even that, it's like I did it for a week, and now I'm out of it again.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我也就用了一个星期，然后又不用了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So is your – you have a big monitor or just a normal monitor?
sentences.zh: 所以你的——你用的是大显示器还是普通显示器？

sentences.en: I have a – it's a big monitor.
sentences.zh: 我用的是一个——大显示器。

sentences.en: It's probably like a 30-inch.
sentences.zh: 大概是个30英寸的。

sentences.en: It's one of these Thunderbolt displays.
sentences.zh: 这是那种雷雳显示器。

sentences.en: So it's like a 4K or 5K or something.
sentences.zh: 所以分辨率大概是4K或5K之类的。

sentences.en: Something like that.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，这样啊。

sentences.en: I think that makes a difference too.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这也有影响。

sentences.en: I don't have any high-resolution ones, so.
sentences.zh: 我没有高分辨率的显示器，所以。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I just – yeah, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 对，我只是——对，我不知道。

sentences.en: I had two monitors at my last job, and I only ended up using one.
sentences.zh: 我上一份工作时有两个显示器，但最后我只用了一个。

sentences.en: The other one was just always just – So the thing I think might solve my problem, but I can never get into it, is the getting like an alternative window manager.
sentences.zh: 另一个总是闲置——所以我觉得能解决我问题、但我却始终用不习惯的东西，是换一个替代的窗口管理器。

sentences.en: So a lot of people use like various like a Haskell – what's the Haskell-based one?
sentences.zh: 很多人会用各种各样的Haskell——那个基于Haskell的叫什么来着？

sentences.en: I always forget.
sentences.zh: 我老是忘。

sentences.en: Why is it slipping my mind?
sentences.zh: 怎么话到嘴边又想不起来了呢？

sentences.en: Anyways, the tiling window managers where you push buttons and you flip your consoles up to corner, your ID over to the left, and it kind of like resizes them automatically.
sentences.zh: 总之，就是那种平铺式窗口管理器，你按几个键就能把控制台甩到角落，把ID移到左边，它会自动帮你调整大小。

sentences.en: Yeah, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，没错。

sentences.en: Based on their positioning.
sentences.zh: 根据它们的位置。

sentences.en: And whenever they show me, it's like, wow, that's really cool.
sentences.zh: 每当他们给我演示的时候，我都觉得，哇，太酷了。

sentences.en: And then I try to use their computer, and I'm like helping them with something.
sentences.zh: 然后当我试着用他们的电脑，比如帮他们弄点什么东西的时候，

sentences.en: I can't make it do anything.
sentences.zh: 我什么都操作不了。

sentences.en: And then, you know, it's like if you only ever use one computer, I guess it's good.
sentences.zh: 然后呢，如果你一直只用一台电脑，那估计挺好的。

sentences.en: But for me, the context switching is so hard.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，上下文切换太难了。

sentences.en: Also, same reason I don't have a lot of aliases in my Bash script.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我的Bash脚本里没有设置很多别名。

sentences.en: So I have like very minimal aliases because when I sit down at someone else's computer and I start – and it's like, oh, it's not working.
sentences.zh: 我的别名极少，因为当我坐在别人的电脑前开始操作时——就会遇到“啊？怎么不管用啊”。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，确实如此。

sentences.en: And then I don't know what the command is because I don't type it.
sentences.zh: 然后我就不知道命令是什么了，因为平时根本不敲它。

sentences.en: Did you switch over to the ohmyzsh after we did that show?
sentences.zh: 我们做完那一期节目后，你换成ohmyzsh了吗？

sentences.en: So I did for my – so actually, you had Baboon.
sentences.zh: 我为我的——其实当时你用的是Baboon。

sentences.en: Was it the same show or a different show?
sentences.zh: 那是同一期节目还是另一期？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，对。

sentences.en: So I use that on a Windows computer now.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在在一台Windows电脑上用那个。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, I have it on there, and I like it.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，我在上面装了，而且我很喜欢。

sentences.en: Except that occasionally it has problems because I get auto-updates.
sentences.zh: 不过偶尔会出问题，因为我会自动更新。

sentences.en: And then like it did like a bad update once, and it took me like an hour just to get back to what I needed.
sentences.zh: 然后它有一次更新翻车了，我花了一个小时才恢复到能用的状态。

sentences.en: And it's like stuff like that just kills me.
sentences.zh: 像这种事简直要了我的命。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But the ohmyzsh, I love the tab completion.
sentences.zh: 不过对于ohmyzsh，我超爱它的Tab键补全功能。

sentences.en: Like I found out the other day it would actually – if you're typing a switch, like a command line argument to a function, it actually has tab completion there.
sentences.zh: 比如我前几天发现它居然能——如果你在输入一个开关，比如某个函数的命令行参数，它连那个都能用Tab键补全。

sentences.en: So when you hit tab, it runs the command with dash dash help.
sentences.zh: 所以当你按下Tab时，它会带上--help参数来运行该命令。

sentences.en: It pulls out all of the switches, and then it tries to complete.
sentences.zh: 它能把所有的开关都提取出来，然后尝试进行补全。

sentences.en: It's like super awesome.
sentences.zh: 这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: That's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 那确实挺酷的。

sentences.en: So I saw the people who do stock trading, and then I think they have the answer to how many monitors.
sentences.zh: 我看到那些做股票交易的人，我觉得他们才真正知道到底该用几个显示器。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, like 100.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，比如100个。

sentences.en: It's like a 3x3 or whatever.
sentences.zh: 就像3x3或者别的什么布局。

sentences.en: So they have like three rows, and it looks like almost like a surround screen.
sentences.zh: 他们有三排屏幕，看起来几乎就像环绕屏一样。

sentences.en: But then I guess you just would go to like a VR, like Oculus Rift, with like total immersion in like a sphere of monitor or something.
sentences.zh: 不过我想你干脆可以直接用VR设备，比如Oculus Rift，完全沉浸在一个显示器构成的球体里之类的。

sentences.en: There's some guy with the Oculus Rift right now who's just banking in the stock market.
sentences.zh: 现在肯定有个戴着Oculus Rift的家伙正在股市里赚大钱呢。

sentences.en: I mean, he's just – every trade is just – he's pulling the one-armed bandit and getting a huge – He is the high-frequency trader.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他只要——每一笔交易都在——他就像在拉老虎机的摇臂，然后大赚一笔——他就是那个高频交易员。

sentences.en: I feel like this is an NBC show coming this fall.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这听起来像是今年秋季要上映的NBC美剧。

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So anyway, so I feel like I need – wherever I is, I always need an additional monitor, but then it's almost not always worth it.
sentences.zh: 总之，不管怎样，我觉得——无论我在哪，我总是需要一个额外的显示器，但转念一想，又往往不太划算。

sentences.en: Some people have like a big monitor and a small monitor, and that's just jarring to me.
sentences.zh: 有些人会用一大一小两个显示器，这让我觉得极其别扭。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, I can't deal with that.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，我可受不了这个。

sentences.en: Or some people have the monitor for reading, like the monitor for reading research papers.
sentences.zh: 或者有些人专门用一个显示器来阅读，比如用来读研究报告的显示器。

sentences.en: Yeah, so portrait and then one – yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，一个竖屏，然后另一个——对。

sentences.en: I don't know why, but that – I think I have like sort of like a OCD when it comes to symmetry on monitors, but I just cannot – I can't even look at that.
sentences.zh: 不知道为什么，我对显示器的对称性有着某种强迫症，我简直——我甚至都无法直视那种布局。

sentences.en: Or the people have mismatched the same size, but like different brands, and so the bezels are different colors.
sentences.zh: 或者有人用的尺寸虽然一样但牌子不同，结果边框颜色都不一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I can't deal with that.
sentences.zh: 对，对，我可接受不了这个。

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I was that kid growing up, though, who if someone – like even if a small corner of the TV screen was blocked by someone's head, I would ask them to move.
sentences.zh: 不过我小时候就是那种小孩，如果有人——哪怕电视屏幕的小小一角被某人的脑袋挡住了，我都会叫他们挪开。

sentences.en: Like, can you please move your head a little bit?
sentences.zh: 比如，能麻烦你把头稍微挪一下吗？

sentences.en: But you're blocking, you know, one one-thousandth of the TV screen.
sentences.zh: 因为你挡住了，你知道的，电视屏幕的千分之一。

sentences.en: So you don't like going to movies then, okay.
sentences.zh: 那你一定不喜欢去电影院了，好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Although, you know, the movie, they do it right.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道，电影院在这方面做得对。

sentences.en: Yeah, the projector is –
sentences.zh: 对，投影仪是——

sentences.en: Stadium seating and projecting it.
sentences.zh: 阶梯式座位加上投影放映。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，没错。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: So on to news.
sentences.zh: 接下来进入新闻环节。

sentences.en: That first article I have is – I didn't look at the guy's name.
sentences.zh: 我看到的头条文章是——我没记那个人的名字。

sentences.en: I think it's Andy Gavin.
sentences.zh: 我想他叫安迪·加文（Andy Gavin）。

sentences.en: Making Crash Bandicoot.
sentences.zh: 制作《古惑狼》（Crash Bandicoot）。

sentences.en: So Crash Bandicoot came out for the PlayStation 1 as, I think, one of the launch titles.
sentences.zh: 《古惑狼》当年作为PlayStation 1的首发游戏之一发售，我想是的。

sentences.en: And this guy, Andy Gavin, was at Naughty Dog.
sentences.zh: 这个叫安迪·加文的人当时在顽皮狗工作。

sentences.en: Well, I guess it was a very new company at the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我猜那时候这还是个非常年轻的公司。

sentences.en: I think they had made one or two games.
sentences.zh: 我想他们当时只做过一两款游戏。

sentences.en: Anyways, and he has a series that I saw linked to off of Reddit or something of like 13 series about writing him and the other guy who were kind of like
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我看到Reddit之类的网站上分享了他写的一个系列，一共13篇，讲的是他和另一个作为顽皮狗核心人物的家伙

sentences.en: the head people at Naughty Dog making Crash Bandicoot and how that like people at the time were just – like I remember playing Crash Bandicoot.
sentences.zh: 是如何制作《古惑狼》的，以及当时的人们——我还记得自己玩《古惑狼》时的情景。

sentences.en: Did you play Crash Bandicoot?
sentences.zh: 你玩过《古惑狼》吗？

sentences.en: I never played it, but I heard about it.
sentences.zh: 我没玩过，但听说过。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，这样啊。

sentences.en: So like at the time, I was a little younger, I guess, so I didn't really realize it was the new PlayStation, right?
sentences.zh: 所以当时我还比较年轻，我猜是这样，所以并没有真正意识到这就是全新的PlayStation，对吧？

sentences.en: Like I just thought this was how everything was going to be now.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得以后所有游戏都会是这个样子的。

sentences.en: But I guess like at the time, it was like one of the very first kind of 3D platformers.
sentences.zh: 但我想当时这可以说是最早的一批3D平台跳跃游戏之一。

sentences.en: And how to do level design, how to get all the textures compressed and how to put things in your field of view that blocked like distant objects
sentences.zh: 以及如何进行关卡设计，如何压缩所有的纹理，以及如何在你的视野中放置物体来遮挡远处的物体

sentences.en: so the number of polygons on screen was reduced.
sentences.zh: 从而减少屏幕上的多边形数量。

sentences.en: All that kind of stuff he goes into in his blog.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的内容都在他的博客里详细写到了。

sentences.en: And like, you know, it's kind of funny when you read it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，读起来还挺逗的。

sentences.en: He says that, you know, for doing like saving space after they had already done all the obvious things, like using the lowest two bits of all the pointers to store data.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，为了在用尽了所有显而易见的方法后进一步节省空间，比如利用所有指针的最低两位来存储数据。

sentences.en: It's like the obvious things.
sentences.zh: 这就像是那些显而易见的操作一样。

sentences.en: Okay, I know.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我知道了。
